source.title: Deep learning and abstractive summarisation for radiological reports: an empirical study for adapting the PEGASUS models' family with scarce data
source.authors: Claudio Benzoni; Martina Langhals; M. Boeker; Luise Modersohn; M. Maros

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation-set summarisation scores during fine-tuning over epochs and reports trajectories that it relates to epoch-wise double descent. It uses validation metrics and a different task and model setup from the original work.
record.gate_note: The study reports validation-set trajectories and early-peak metric values for fine-tuning over epochs. It does not evaluate a test split; the authors defer that evaluation. Results cited from other papers are not recorded as rows. The PEGASUS-X model-size comparison is recorded under fits_no_version because it does not test the full model-wise double-descent curve.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes pretrained PEGASUS summarisation models on radiology reports and tracks validation scores over 300 epochs. Its results bear on V2, epoch-wise double descent, in a new setting: pretrained encoder-decoder fine-tuning, validation summarisation metrics rather than test error, and no training-error or interpolation measurement. The authors only conjecture the link to epoch-wise double descent and also call it catastrophic forgetting. T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, with three qualifications. The authors frame the PEGASUS pattern mainly as catastrophic forgetting followed by recovery. They only conjecture it is a case of epoch-wise double descent. They attribute the weaker larger PEGASUS-X checkpoint partly to its long-input pretraining objective, not only to its size.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained encoder-decoder summarisation checkpoints on radiology reports and tracks validation summarisation metrics; it is not a controlled test of test error around an interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trajectory varies with model checkpoint and training-subset size; PEGASUS-X base is nearly monotonic, while PEGASUS runs show peak-drop-recovery on the larger subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: On the full training subset, best validation ROUGE-1 is 0.6505 for pegasus-x-base and 0.5687 for pegasus-x-large. The two also differ in pretraining objective fit, not only size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In scarce-data fine-tuning, a larger pretrained checkpoint can underperform a smaller one.

fits_no_version.finding: At the early peak, outputs are mostly negated diagnoses or empty strings; in binary classification, xsum-100% scores precision 0.62 and recall 0.94, near a dummy classifier. So the first peak reflects a degenerate majority-class solution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The early peak in fine-tuning metric curves can reflect trivial outputs rather than generalisation.

record.code_released: not stated (code can be made available by reasonable request)
record.problems: The study reports validation rather than test-split results, and the authors defer test-set evaluation. It uses one dataset and one model family, and the evaluation is automated despite the authors noting limitations of such metrics. The reported PEGASUS-X parameter counts differ between Methods and Results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out. Table 2's binary classification of generated summaries is not a measure of test error or epoch-wise generalization curves.

untested.parts: Test error, training error and interpolation timing; behaviour beyond 300 epochs for the 10% subset; dependence on label noise.
No test of sample size near an interpolation threshold.

missing.what: Onset epochs of the third (recovery) phase: large-50% at 106, large-100% at 48, xsum-50% at 65, xsum-100% at 32.
Best validation ROUGE-1 in the recovery phase for PEGASUS: pegasus/large 0.6027 at epoch 213, pegasus/xsum 0.6323 at epoch 257. These quantify recovery above the early peak.
PEGASUS-X base epochs to reach 95% of final ROUGE-1: 134, 60, 29 for the 10%, 50%, 100% subsets.

record.verdict_notes: Measures are higher-is-better validation scores, so peak-drop-recovery corresponds to an error fall-rise-fall. No training error or interpolation point is reported. The test split is not evaluated. There is a single run per setting with no uncertainty estimate. Table 1 and the text disagree on the large-50% peak epoch (23 vs 12).

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep establishing a fall-rise-fall curve or locating a peak near interpolation.
Direct test error; results use validation-set summarisation metrics and do not assess whether the peak occurs near interpolation.
No test-error comparison near an interpolation threshold as training sample size increases.
Only PEGASUS-family summarisation models are studied; no general comparison across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated.
No label-noise or regularization sweep, and no test of multiple peaks or their disappearance under optimal regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters.

relationships.condition: pegasus-large and pegasus-xsum fine-tuned on 50% and 100% subsets
relationships.reason: Validation scores show an early peak, a sharp drop with gibberish outputs, then a later phase exceeding the early peak (e.g., large-100% ROUGE-1 0.3625 early vs best 0.6027). This is validation-only and the authors only conjecture it is double descent (r5-r12, r17-r24).
relationships.display_finding: Validation scores peaked early, dropped sharply with gibberish outputs, and later exceeded the early peak, including pegasus-large ROUGE-1 improving from 0.3625 to 0.6027 on the 100% subset.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: pegasus-large and pegasus-xsum fine-tuned on 50% and 100% subsets
source_check.reason: §4.1 explicitly reports an early score peak, degradation and later scores exceeding the early peak for all four runs; these are validation metrics.

relationships.condition: pegasus-large and pegasus-xsum on the 10% subset (268 examples)
relationships.reason: Scores rise then degrade, with no recovery within 300 epochs. The authors only extrapolate that recovery would come after more than 530 or 330 epochs (r1-r4, r13-r16).
relationships.display_finding: Scores rose then degraded without recovery within 300 epochs; recovery beyond 530 or 330 epochs was extrapolated rather than observed.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: pegasus-large and pegasus-xsum on the 10% subset (268 examples)
source_check.reason: The observed trajectory is incomplete within 300 epochs: improvement followed by degradation without recovery. Recovery beyond 530 or 330 epochs is conjectural.

relationships.reason: The authors report a nearly monotonic increase with no peak-drop-recovery, so the effect depends on the checkpoint (r25-r27).
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased nearly monotonically across all subsets, without a peak, drop, and recovery.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: §4.2 explicitly describes nearly monotonic improvement across subsets, qualifying the checkpoint scope of the effect observed in PEGASUS.

tranche.reason: Reports an epoch-wise peak-drop-recovery trajectory in a new setting: pretrained encoder-decoder fine-tuning for radiological summarization.

source_check.notes: Table 1 values are scores at ROUGE-1-selected early peaks; trajectory states depend on the accompanying text. Table 1 gives large-50% peak epoch 23 despite prose suggesting 12; pegasus-x-base parameter counts conflict between §3.3 (272 million) and §4.2 (257 million).

statements.correction: §4.1: qualitative output inspection; Table 2: binary-classification analysis benchmarked against a dummy classifier with precision 0.62 and recall 1.0. §8: code available on reasonable request. No controlled double-descent mechanism experiment or uncertainty estimates reported.
statements.problem: The trajectory description is correct, but the unqualified absence of code, controls and capability checks overlooks code availability on request and the auxiliary output and classification analyses.
